This is first application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of regular bail relating to FIR/Crime No.176/2023 dated 15.04.2023 registered at Police Station Chhipawada, District Harda (M.P.) for the offences punishable under Sections 363, 366,
376(3), 376(2)(n) of IPC and Section 5/6 of the POCSO Act, 2012.
Learned counsel for applicant has submitted that applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the crime in question.

sentences.text: The applicant is in custody since 29.01.2024 and trial will take considerable time to conclude.
sentences._hearing_file: Umesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 June, 2024.json

sentences.text: He further submits that applicant is permanent resident of district and there is no likelihood of his absconding from the clutches of law or tampering with prosecution evidence.
sentences._hearing_file: Umesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 June, 2024.json

sentences.text: He also submits that the applicant is ready to furnish adequate surety and shall abide by all the directions and conditions which may be imposed by this Court.
sentences._hearing_file: Umesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 June, 2024.json

sentences.text: Upon these grounds, the applicant may be released on bail.
sentences._hearing_file: Umesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 June, 2024.json

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case-diary.

sentences.text: This bail application has been argued on the ground that a child has been born to the prosecutrix and to provide proper care and protection to the 2 MCRC-22425-2024 prosecutrix and the child, the applicant should be released on bail.
sentences._hearing_file: Umesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 June, 2024.json

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the State has opposed the bail application on the ground that the prosecutrix was below 16 years of age at the time of incident and she was subjected to sexual abuse.
sentences._hearing_file: Umesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 June, 2024.json

sentences.text: Taking these facts into consideration, this bail application is dismissed.

opennyai_summary.final__facts:
Order 
This is second bail application filed by the applicant under Section 483 of the Bharatiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (Section 439 of Cr.P.C.) for grant of regular bail relating to FIR/Crime No.176/2023 dated 15.04.2023 registered at Police Station Chhipawada District Harda for the offence punishable under Sections 363, 366, 376(3), 376(2)(n) of IPC and Section 5/6 of POCSO Act.
opennyai_summary.final__arguments:
2. Learned counsel for the applicant contends that the statement of victim has been recorded before the trial Court.
Victim has turned hostile.
She has not supported the allegation levelled against the present applicant.
3. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent has opposed the prayer and submitted that offence has been committed upon the victim.
DNA report is positive and therefore, the testimony of the prosecutrix recorded before the trial Court, automatic becomes suspicious as the prosecutrix is denying the factum of relationship with the present applicant.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Having considered the submission perusal of record and the fact that so far as the present applicant is concerned, prosecutrix has not alleged anything against the present applicant.
The applicant is aged about 21 years and he is in custody since 29.01.2024.
Thus, taking into consideration the prolong period of custody and also age of the applicant, this Court is of the considered view that it is a fit case to release the applicant on bail.
